(1) /app/backend/requirements.txt installed cleanly in a FRESH python3.11 venv (/tmp/freshvenv) with no errors; `import cryptography, aiomysql, pymysql, fastapi` all succeed (cryptography 50.0.2, aiomysql 0.2.0, PyMySQL 1.1.1 per pip, fastapi 0.110.1). critical_code_review_comments: requirements.txt pins are consistent: cryptography==50.0.2 depends on cffi>=1.12 (cffi==2.1.1 satisfies) which depends on pycparser (pycparser==3.0 satisfies). Pins are internally compatible.
PyMySQL 1.1.1 + cryptography>=3.3 is the officially supported combination for caching_sha2_password (MySQL 8.x default auth). Confirmed working against real MySQL 8.4.8.
Minor: pip reports PyMySQL 1.1.1 as installed (pin honored) though pymysql.__version__ shows '1.4.6' due to upstream module-level version string; functionally correct and non-blocking.

Consider adding a smoke test in CI that spins up MySQL 8.x with caching_sha2_password to prevent future regressions of this exact class of bug (the local-preview MariaDB with mysql_native_password masked it).

rca of the issue: MySQL 8.x defaults to caching_sha2_password. PyMySQL dispatches this auth to the `cryptography` package via cffi; if cryptography is not importable at runtime, PyMySQL raises RuntimeError and the connection (and thus the FastAPI startup) fails -> container crash-loop. Local preview used MariaDB with mysql_native_password so the missing dep was invisible. Fix: pin cryptography==50.0.2 (+ transitive cffi==2.1.1, pycparser==3.0) in /app/backend/requirements.txt so the Docker image installs them. Verified end-to-end against a real MySQL 8.4.8 instance with the crm user explicitly created using WITH caching_sha2_password.
